speaker: NARRATOR
text: San Francisco. The 1950s. Two heart doctors, Meyer Friedman and Ray Rosenman, have a waiting room problem.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Their chairs need fixing. So they call in an upholsterer.

speaker: UPHOLSTERER
text: [looking the chairs over, puzzled] Huh. [beat] What kind of patients do you got in here, doc?

speaker: FRIEDMAN
text: [busy, clipped, not looking up] Heart patients. Why?

speaker: UPHOLSTERER
text: [matter-of-fact] 'Cause they only wear out the front of the seat. [taps the chair] Look. Nobody in here ever sits back.

speaker: YOU
text: [small laugh] ...That's me in every waiting room.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Nobody sat back. They perched. On the edge. Ready to spring up.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: As Friedman later told the story, that was the moment it clicked. Maybe the people getting heart disease... had something in common.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Always on the edge of the seat.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: They gave it a name you've definitely heard.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And for a while... it looked like a breakthrough.
